correctness.rationale: A tuple of k subsets colors each atom by a q=2^k symbol; each σ-cycle gives an oriented cyclic word. Every term reduces to Boolean combinations of finitely many σ^j(A_i). A minterm e_w identifies whether a word occurs in any position; therefore two tuples have the same complete qf type precisely when their sets of occurring length-d necklaces agree. Every nonempty necklace support of size at most m occurs, giving T_k=Σ_{j≤min(m,N_d(q))}C(N_d(q),j). Full automorphisms C_d wr S_m preserve necklace MULTISETS, giving the separate stars-and-bars orbit count; support fixes multiset iff m≤2, and distinct multiplicity assignments show failure already unary at m≥3. Burnside gives N_d and asymptotic leading term T_k~2^{kdm}/(d^m m!), whose reciprocal coefficient is strictly increasing in m for fixed n=dm≥3; n=2 gives sole collision {(1,2),(2,1)}. Independent complete color enumerations for eight (d,m,k) cases reproduced both qf-type and orbit counts, including the n=2 collision. This finite evidence does not replace the all-k proof.
residual_risks: The intended equivalence is for parameter-free quantifier-free types in the full Boolean-operation plus named-σ language, and only uniform cycle lengths.
Numerical type-spectrum collision is not a syntactic-type identification across different underlying algebras.
